qualifying_findings.title: AgentScope MCP workspace command injection, agent-service missing authentication, and bash-tool authorization error
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: GitHub Advisory Database publication; public researcher disclosure and public upstream issue/pull-request references
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: AgentScope agent service through 2.0.11 for the MCP workspace command injection and missing authentication; bash-tool authorization issue through 2.0.8, with 2.0.9 reported as its fixed release.
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: The published CVE-2026-123022 advisory states that an externally supplied MCP Workspace API command reaches subprocess.Popen without adequate neutralization, allowing remote OS command injection. The same November 5 disclosure group reports a missing-authentication condition on the agent service and an authorization error in the bash tool. The command-injection advisory says its remediation pull request awaited acceptance at publication; the public disclosure distinguishes the bash-tool fix from the two still-unreleased fixes.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: An agent-service MCP configuration endpoint is a delegated-execution boundary. Missing authentication or unsafe command construction lets an untrusted network caller choose a process executed with the service account's agent and tool authority.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: AgentScope product background belongs in ai-wiki; general coding-agent service practice belongs in ai-dev-wiki. Retain the concrete MCP execution, authentication, authorization, affected-version, and mitigation evidence locally.
qualifying_findings.confidence: high for CVE-2026-123022 publication and command-injection facts; medium for grouped related-CVE remediation detail pending direct maintainer-authored advisory pages for all three.
follow_up_actions: Verify each related GHSA and its exact fixed-version field before durable synthesis.
Until a maintainer release fixes the MCP workspace surface, restrict it to trusted network paths or disable it when unused.
Do not convert the advisory's public-exploit wording into evidence of active exploitation.

qualifying_findings.title: Dagu MCP DAG-specification read bypasses path containment and workspace isolation
qualifying_findings.evidence_classification: Public CVE-record publication dated November 5; linked project security advisory, patch discussion, commit, and release evidence
qualifying_findings.affected_boundary_or_version: Dagu before 2.11.0; MCP dagu_read operation with target dag_spec, requiring a viewer-role API key and a readable YAML target.
qualifying_findings.factual_summary: The CVE record says Dagu's MCP dagu_read DAG-specification path calls the API in process and bypasses an HTTP-only traversal guard. A viewer-role API key can supply an absolute or traversing path to read accessible .yaml or .yml files outside configured DAG directories. The record identifies v2.11.0 as the fix and does not establish write or command-execution capability.
qualifying_findings.why_it_matters_for_ai_security: MCP read tools are data-authorization boundaries. A transport-specific path check can leave a tool path able to disclose workflow definitions, configuration, or secrets outside the agent's intended workspace.
qualifying_findings.upstream_routing: Dagu product background belongs in ai-wiki; general workflow-engine development practice belongs in ai-dev-wiki. Retain this MCP path-containment, authorization, affected-version, and patch evidence locally.
qualifying_findings.confidence: high for the CVE-record date, affected version, read-only boundary, and v2.11.0 remediation; no active exploitation claim is supported by the retained sources.
follow_up_actions: Confirm that deployments expose dagu_read only to intended viewer principals and upgrade to v2.11.0 or later.
Review readable YAML files for credentials and rotate any potentially exposed material.
During ingest, confirm the release and patch apply the guard at the shared storage boundary rather than only one transport.
